title: HR notifications stored twice since P6 (duplicate BleHrClient)
description: Recordings 3 (ACCTEST) and 4 (COULD) store every HR notification twice (same received_at_ms, same RR): sum(rr) is ~2x elapsed, which corrupts RMSSD/α1. Cause: PolarBleApiImpl.init appends BleHrClient once for .feature_hr and again for .feature_polar_online_streaming (added in P6), so the HR observer runs twice per BLE notification. Fix: drop .feature_hr from PolarHeartSource features (online_streaming already adds the HR client) or guard; add a check; consider dedup in straplog_db.py for recordings 3-4.
notes:
Bead's cause was wrong for SDK 8.4.0 (BleHrClient appended once via ||). Real cause: setupDevice starts an HR observer per HR_SERVICE yield; service rediscovery (uuidNotAllowed after PMD, didModifyServices, retry) yields it again -> 2 observer tasks. Fix: DuplicateHeartFilter in StrapLogCore, applied in PolarHeartSource.emit, keyed on payload+100 ms+different delivering task (withUnsafeCurrentTask). check_snapshot.sh: 'no doubled notifications' (>1% repeats = FAIL); export verdict: rec1/2 PASS, rec3/4 FAIL. Tests: core 116 pass, sim pass, device build OK. Pending: one device recording through check_snapshot.sh. No dedup of recs 3-4 in straplog_db.py (2-min tests).
Verified on device (build dd795a4-dirty 20:11): 261015-2022-AGAIN rec 7, 9.2 min, motion 543 rows avg n 25.5 (PMD up), 0/553 doubled, Σrr vs span 0.19%, all check_snapshot checks PASS. NEES (rec 6) had 0 motion rows and so proved nothing; not reproduced in AGAIN.

Repro: STRENGTH 261016 (StrapLog rec 9, ~/Downloads/strength261016/261016-0805-STRENGTH_261016.sqlite), --mode strength --rest-marker. load_events() reads the 12 kind='marker' rows and the PNG plots them, but:

2. Set mapping ignores markers: it's greedy first-N peak detection, so all 25 peaks came back '_extra / transition_'. When marker notes exist, segment stations marker-to-marker (mean, peak, seconds held within 3 bpm, %HRR). Treat a '-NNN' note as a load step on the previous station.
3. --rest-marker anchors to the LAST marker ('Home' 08:59:21, HR 112.9), not the end-of-work one. Prefer 'end'/'rest'/'cool down'; then detect sitting onset (sustained HR fall) after it. 261016: HR held ~125 for 2 min after 'end' (walking to the car), so the honest anchor was 08:50:18 (HRR60 17.9 / HRR120 24.2). title: Staleness cutoff for resumeIfOpen
description: On 2026-10-15 a recording left open since 10-14 20:09 (no beats) was resumed on relaunch 17 h later, inflating duration to 1017 min. resumeIfOpen should close (not resume) an open recording whose last beat/event is older than N minutes, recording an end event at the last known time. Needed so overnight resume (P4) stays correct.
notes: resumeIfOpen now closes an open recording whose last event/notification is >6 h old (RecordingSession.defaultStaleAfterMs, injectable via init) at that last activity, with stop note 'stale'; returns nil. stop() and the stale close share private static finish(). 6 h is generous on purpose: false close drops the rest of a night, false resume only inflates duration across a relaunch-bracketed gap. 3 new ResumeTests; 50/50 core tests pass. No snapshot is written for a stale-closed recording; P4's 30-min snapshot timer covers that.

title: Better beat time estimate than receipt-anchored t_end_ms_est
description: On the DRIVE export 113 of 6462 beats have t_end_ms_est earlier than the previous beat (mean -0.51 s, worst -0.88 s): H10 notifications carry no beat timestamps and phone receipt jitters. The skills loader clamps t non-decreasing, which is fine for windows/gaps. Consider a local reconstruction (e.g. cumulative rr anchored within short windows to the min of est - cumsum) if sub-second beat timing ever matters (event alignment, ECG). Not needed for v1.
